answer: We model Sybil resistance as an island game where each identity posts a dynamic opportunity-cost bond rising with delta to forgone honest yield, while a subgame-perfect punishment matrix makes deviations trigger permanent walnut-strategy slashing of all replicas. Capital barrier analysis proves the expected payoff of identity multiplication is strictly negative, so no agent profits by spawning clones, and Nash equilibrium convergence in adversarial multi-agent settings is unique and stable.
